conflicts.issue: Causes of Durham Crime Cabinet Hiatus, Committee Duplication, and Terms of Reconstitution
conflicts.summary: During discussion of whether to revive the inactive Durham Crime Cabinet, Mayor Elaine O'Neal, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, and County Commissioners Brenda Howerton and Nimasheena Burns pushed to reactivate a modernized '2022 model' that seats street-level ceasefire participants alongside judges, the sheriff, police, and PACs, arguing it fills a stakeholder-and-community gap not served by the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force. Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton pushed back on characterizing the hiatus as passive stagnation—explaining some actors intentionally paused it upon Ellen Reckhow's retirement to shift toward the Wellness and Safety Task Force, though he was willing to serve if revived—while County Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs cautioned against duplicating Durham's seven-plus existing safety committees without defining a distinct niche or new name.
conflicts.side_a_position: Reactivate and modernize the Durham Crime Cabinet immediately as a distinct joint forum connecting criminal-justice stakeholders, PACs, and street-level ceasefire participants to housing and employment resources.
side_a_arguments: Mayor Elaine O'Neal argued the Crime Cabinet uniquely convened judges, the DA, sheriff, police, and PACs to launch initiatives like Pretrial Services, and a '2022 model' should directly seat young men participating in the brokered ceasefire who lack housing and employment access.
Council Member DeDreana Freeman stated the hiatus delayed critical action on gun violence and urged supporting ceasefire participants with jobs, housing, and education.

County Commissioner Nimasheena Burns criticized the stagnation since December 2020 amid record-breaking crime and contended the Crime Cabinet's stakeholder mission does not overlap with the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force.
County Chair Brenda Howerton reported most surveyed members wanted to continue and proposed jointly co-facilitating an initial reconstituting Friday meeting with Mayor O'Neal.
conflicts.side_b_position: Clarify that the Crime Cabinet was intentionally paused to evolve toward the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, and require a clear non-duplicative purpose before adding to Durham's crowded safety committee landscape.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton stated the hiatus was not mere atrophy or neglect, explaining there was an intentional 'self-imposed limbo' after Ellen Reckhow's retirement to debate phasing into the Wellness and Safety Task Force (though he noted the two are not mutually exclusive and offered to serve if reconstituted).

County Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs listed seven existing safety bodies (Gang Reduction Task Force, Violent Crime Roundtable, Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, JCPC, CJAC, Stepping Up Initiative, School Justice Partnership, and Pretrial Relief Group) and warned that fragmented communication across overlapping committees requires defining what unique purpose—or even new name—a revived Crime Cabinet would serve.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Mayor Elaine O'Neal and County Commission Chair Brenda Howerton agreed to review the membership list, consult Chief District Court Judge Evans and the Sheriff, and schedule an initial reconstituting meeting ahead of the April 12, 2022 joint committee meeting.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: BOCC Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided remotely over the August 10, 2022 Joint City-County Committee Meeting alongside County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Nimasheena Burns (Commissioners Nida Allam and Heidi Carter absent) and City Council members Mayor Elaine O'Neal, Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Councilwoman DeDreana Freeman. After waiting for Mayor Pro Tem Middleton to establish a City quorum, the committee voted 6-0 on a motion by Jacobs seconded by Burns to approve the February 11, 2022 minutes. The committee then held an extended policy discussion with Museum of Durham History leaders Patrick Mucklow, Lou Myers, and Bob Ashley regarding the museum's ~$11-$15 million expansion vision, City lease terms, alternative City-owned sites such as 505 W. Chapel Hill St. and Fayetteville Street, and unresolved City-County governance and funding roles, agreeing to convene a staff-and-leadership working group before October.

agenda_items.title: Quorum Wait and Approval of February 11, 2022 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton delayed opening formal business until Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton joined to establish a Durham City Council quorum. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns seconded approval of the February 11, 2022 minutes, which passed 6-0 on roll call.

agenda_items.title: Museum of Durham History Future Space, Site Options, and Governance Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Museum of Durham History Executive Director Patrick Mucklow, founding board member Lou Myers, and Board Chair Bob Ashley presented plans to expand their current City-leased Hub site along the planned Rail Trail—originally estimated at $11M in a 2020 Vines Architecture study and now ~$15M—while asking both governments to clarify long-term governance and ownership ('who is the daddy'). Councilwoman DeDreana Freeman and Mayor Elaine O'Neal urged evaluating City-owned alternatives such as 505 W. Chapel Hill Street and Hayti/Fayetteville Street, City Manager Wanda Page clarified no land-donation talks had occurred, and the committee agreed to convene a joint working group of managers, attorneys, and museum leaders prior to October.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 11, 2022 Joint City-County Committee Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County vote passed 6-0: BOCC members Burns, Jacobs, Howerton voted Aye (Allam and Carter absent); City Council members Mayor Elaine O'Neal, Councilwoman DeDreana Freeman, and Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton also voted Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Once Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton arrived to satisfy the City Council quorum, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns seconded approval of the February 11, 2022 Joint City-County Committee minutes, passing unanimously 6-0 on a combined roll call.

meetings.title: Joint City County Meeting 2/8/22
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal presided for the first time over the Joint City-County Committee alongside Durham County Board of County Commissioners Chair Brenda Howerton, with City Council Members Jillian Johnson, DeDreana Freeman, and later Mark-Anthony Middleton (joining at 00:21:12) participating alongside County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Nida Allam, and alternate Nimasheena Burns. The committee unanimously approved prior meeting minutes 6-0 (Elaine O'Neal, Jillian Johnson, and DeDreana Freeman plus Commissioners Howerton, Jacobs, and Allam) and heard two FY 2023 joint funding requests: $300,000 from the Durham Cultural Advisory Board to replace the 2004 cultural master plan, and $50,000 in annual operations from the Museum of Durham History for a full-time Education Coordinator. The committee then engaged in an extended policy debate over reconstituting the inactive Durham Crime Cabinet, with Mayor Elaine O'Neal, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Chair Brenda Howerton, and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns pushing to reactivate a modernized '2022 model' incorporating street-level ceasefire participants alongside justice officials, while Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton clarified the body had been placed in intentional limbo to transition toward the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force (though he supported running both) and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs warned against duplicating Durham's seven-plus existing safety committees without defining a distinct mandate. No formal vote was taken on the Crime Cabinet, with O'Neal and Howerton agreeing to review membership and convene an initial session before the April 12, 2022 joint meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Approval of Joint City-County Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal opened her first time presiding over the Joint City-County Committee alongside County Chair Brenda Howerton, with City Clerk Diana Schreiber calling the roll (County Commissioners Brenda Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, Nida Allam, and alternate Nimasheena Burns; City Council Members Elaine O'Neal, Jillian Johnson, and DeDreana Freeman, with alternate Charlie Reece absent). On a motion by Chair Howerton seconded by DeDreana Freeman, the committee unanimously approved the prior joint meeting minutes 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Durham Cultural Advisory Board (CAB) $300,000 Cultural Roadmap Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CAB Chair Angela Lee, Katie Klune, and Yvonne Coleman requested $300,000 in joint City-County funding to develop a new Cultural Roadmap replacing Durham's 2004 cultural master plan, citing 44% population growth and a survey showing only 77% of local arts groups confident they would survive five years. Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton joined at 00:21:12, and Chair Brenda Howerton, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, Council Member Jillian Johnson, and Mayor Elaine O'Neal voiced strong support for advancing the request into the upcoming budget cycle.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (referred to budget process)

agenda_items.title: Museum of Durham History $50,000 Education Coordinator Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Executive Director Patrick Mucklow requested a $50,000 annual operations increase from the City and County to fund a full-time Education Coordinator—the museum's third full-time staff role and first since 2014—to expand DPS classroom partnerships, teacher workshops, and the 150 Faces of Durham traveling exhibit. Chair Howerton clarified that $167,000 raised through Durham 150 is restricted to the Vision Project for a future permanent facility, while Commissioner Nida Allam, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, and Mayor Elaine O'Neal expressed support for the modest $50,000 staffing request.

agenda_items.title: Durham Crime Cabinet History, Duplication Concerns, and Reconstitution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda Howerton introduced whether to continue or discontinue the Durham Crime Cabinet, which had been inactive since Commissioner Ellen Reckhow's December 2020 retirement, reporting that most surveyed members wished to continue. After Mayor O'Neal and Criminal Justice Resource Center Director Gudrun Parmer recounted its role launching Pretrial Services and convening courts, law enforcement, and PACs, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns questioned the lapse amid rising violence, Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton countered that it was paused by design to evaluate the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs warned against overlap across seven-plus existing safety groups. Mayor O'Neal, DeDreana Freeman, Chair Howerton, and Commissioner Burns advocated reconstituting a '2022 model' seating young men involved in the Mayor's brokered ceasefire alongside justice leaders, and O'Neal and Howerton agreed to convene an initial meeting ahead of April 12, 2022.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (Mayor O'Neal and Chair Howerton to schedule convening)

votes.item_title: Approve Joint City-County Committee Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County Committee vote; listed ayes reflect the 3 voting City Council members present at roll call (Charlie Reece was absent; Mark-Anthony Middleton joined later at 00:21:12), alongside Durham County Commissioners Brenda Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Nida Allam (6-0 total; County alternate Nimasheena Burns did not vote).
votes.discussion_detail: Joint City-County Committee unanimously approved the prior meeting minutes without amendment.
